![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14227715/assets/c85e6ee974a59d956367634fdd1d57b65e9d42a980fe1750886527b173f05d32.png)

Find $BM$ given that the area of $△ACB$ is $49\,{cm}^{2},$ $AM=5\,cm,$ and $MC=9\,cm.$

(Figure not drawn to scale)
question.worked_solution:
The area of the triangle is defined as 

$$
A=\frac{b\cdot h}{2},
$$

 where $b$ is the base and $h$ is the corresponding height.

From the diagram, we see that the height is $h=BM,$ and the corresponding base is 

$$
b=AM+MC=14\,cm.
$$

Therefore, using the formula for the area, we can solve for the height as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{b\cdot h}{2} \\ 49 & =\frac{14\cdot h}{2} \\ 98 & =14\cdot h \\ h & =\frac{98}{14} \\ h & =7\,cm\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $BM=7\,\text{cm}.$
